entries.name: Absorptive
entries: When you are wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, damage that you take from weapons is reduced by an amount equal to the absorptive number. If this would reduce the damage to 0, the damage is instead reduced to 1.

entries.name: Slug Cartridge
entries: Weapons with this property fire slug cartridges, which must be loaded in order to fire the weapon.

entries.name: Agile
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, your Dexterity score becomes equal to the agile number. If your Dexterity is already equal to or greater than the agile number, it has no effect on you.

entries.name: Anchor
entries: A {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property can be used to {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|provide cover}. As an action, you can anchor or recover the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. While anchored, you gain no benefit from a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, and it does not require the use of a hand. Instead, while anchored, a light {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} provides one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, a medium {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} provides {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover}, and a heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} provides three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

entries.name: Strength
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with the strength property, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by 10 unless your Strength score meets or exceeds the strength number.

entries.name: Auto
entries: Weapons with this property can only fire in burst, penetrating, or rapid modes. If the weapon has any combination of burst, penetrating, and rapid modes, you choose which mode to use. You can only use one mode at a time.

entries.name: Avoidant
entries: When wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and a creature makes an attack against you, the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range decreases by an amount equal to the avoidant number, to a minimum of 1.

entries.name: Barbed
entries: When you succeed on a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to initiate or maintain a grapple while wearing armor with this property, the creature takes kinetic damage using the barbed damage (which appears in parentheses with the property) + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Biting
entries: This weapon's damage becomes acid. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with a weapon with the biting property, you can instead force the target to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon, or the biting number, whichever is lower). If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes normal weapon damage and is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and the first attack it makes before the end of its next turn has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. If damage dealt by this weapon reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a DC 13 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing and carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Bulky
entries: While wearing armor with this property, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound.

entries.name: Bright
entries: This weapon's damage becomes fire, and its luminous property sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet while activated, instead of only dim light in a 5-foot radius. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with a weapon with the bright property, you can instead force the target to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon, or the bright number, whichever is lower). If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes normal weapon damage and is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and the creature takes additional damage of the same type at the start of its next turn equal to your governing ability modifier.

entries.name: Brutal
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a weapon with the brutal property, you roll a number of additional weapon damage dice equal to the brutal number.

entries.name: Burst
entries: When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with this property, you can instead spray a 10-foot-cube area within range with shots, consuming ammunition equal to the burst number. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or take the weapon's normal damage. Before you use this property, you can declare one creature that would be affected by it. If the creature fails its save, in addition to the weapon's normal damage, it is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit. If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Charging
entries: When you take damage while wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you gain a charge. You can store a maximum number of charges equal to the charging number, and the charges last for 1 minute. The next time you hit with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} while you have charges, you deal additional damage of the same type as the weapon's damage equal to the number of charges stored, and the charges are expended.

entries.name: Concealing
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Corruption
entries: This weapon's damage becomes necrotic, and it loses the luminous property if it has it. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with a weapon with the corruption property, you can instead force the target to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon, or the corruption number, whichever is lower). If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes normal weapon damage and is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and the creature cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Cumbersome
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by 5.

entries.name: Double
entries: A weapon with this property can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property—the damage when the weapon is used with Double-Weapon Fighting. See the rules for Double-Weapon Fighting in chapter 9.

entries.name: Defensive
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn with a weapon with the defensive property, you can choose to suffer a penalty to attack and damage rolls with that weapon up to the defensive number. If you do so, you gain the same bonus to AC. These effects last until the start of your next turn, as long as you're holding the weapon.

entries.name: Dexterity
entries: A weapon with this property requires more skill to control. While wielding it, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} unless you meet the Dexterity requirement.

entries.name: Dire
entries: Before you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the dire property, you can choose to suffer a penalty to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} up to the dire number. If you do so and you hit with it, you gain an equivalent bonus to the damage roll.

entries.name: Disarming
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a weapon with the disarming property against a creature that is holding an object, you can attempt to disarm the target (no action required). If the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or it drops an object of your choice at its feet.

entries.name: Disintegrate
entries: When a creature is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} by a weapon with the disintegrate property, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the disintegrate number. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing or carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Disruptive
entries: When a creature is forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} due to taking damage from a weapon with the disruptive property, the DC for the check equals 10 or the full damage taken, whichever number is higher, instead of only half.

entries.name: Disguised
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) checks made to hide the nature of a weapon with this property.

entries.name: Fixed
entries: A weapon with this property does not fill the hand, but you can't use the weapon while the hand is full. Additionally, you have a +10 bonus to {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being disarmed of this weapon.

entries.name: Gauntleted
entries: While wearing armor with this property, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal kinetic damage using the gauntleted damage (which appears in parentheses with the property) + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Hidden
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight Of Hand|sw5e-phb}) checks made to conceal a weapon with this property.

entries.name: Imbalanced
entries: When you are critically hit while wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can't take reactions until the start of your next turn, and you gain no AC benefit from your {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} against the next attack against you before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Impermeable
entries: 2 Armor with this property includes the limited functions of a number of enviromental suits equal the impermeable number from the list below, which are either included in parentheses with the property or determined by the GM. Additionally, it includes 4 hours' capacity of oxygen, which can be replenished by oxygen tanks.

items: {@b Chemical Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Corroded|sw5e-phb|corroded} condition.
{@b Conductive Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} condition.

{@b Dampening Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} condition, and you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound.
{@b Diving Suit:} You are protected from the hazards associated with high pressure environments.
{@b Flame-Proof Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Ignited|sw5e-phb|ignited} condition.
{@b Hazard Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} condition.

{@b Mind-Shielding Suit:} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid having your mind read or affected.
{@b Space Suit:} You are protected from the hazards associated with low pressure environments.

{@b Stabilizer Suit:} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being moved.

entries.name: Interlocking
entries: While wielding a weapon with the interlocking property, you can use your object interaction to detach the weapon into two separate weapons or reattach into a single weapon. While separated, each weapon has the same damage, damage type, combined value and weight, and properties (except for the double property) as the single weapon.

entries.name: Insulated
entries: When you make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect that would deal ion or lightning damage while wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of below the insulated number as the insulated number.

entries.name: Interlocking
entries: While wielding a weapon with the interlocking property, you can use your object interaction to detach the weapon into two separate weapons or reattach into a single weapon. While separated, each weapon has the same damage, damage type, combined value and weight, and properties (except for the double property) as the single weapon.

entries.name: Keen
entries: When you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the keen property, the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range increases by an amount equal to the keen number.

entries.name: Lambent
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to activate or deactivate the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}'s light. While active, the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet. Additionally, Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made while the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}'s light is active that rely on sight have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Lightweight
entries: Armor and shields with this property have their weight reduced by half.

entries.name: Luminous
entries: A weapon with this property sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius while activated. Additionally, Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made while the weapon is activated have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Magnetic
entries: While you are wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} misses you by an amount less than or equal to your bonus to AC from your {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, the attacking creature must make a Strength check, DC equal to the magnetic number. On a failed save, the creature's weapon adheres to the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. As an action, a creature can repeat this check. On a success, the weapon is freed.

entries.name: Mighty
entries: When making an attack with a mighty weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

entries.name: Modal
entries: A weapon with this property can switch between modes. A list of weapons in parentheses appears with the property-the weapons between which an exotic weapon can be switched by using an object interaction.

entries.name: Neuralizing
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon with the neuralizing property, you can force it to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the neuralizing number. On a failed save, the creature takes an additional 1d4 psychic damage and becomes {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Obscured
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, electronic sensors and cameras have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks against you that rely on sight.

entries.name: Obtrusive
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Power Cell
entries: Weapons with this property are fueled by {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, which must be loaded in order to fire the weapon. A {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} fuels a number of attacks equal to the weapon's reload number.

entries.name: Penetrating
entries: When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with this property, you can instead attempt to penetrate and hit a creature behind the target, consuming ammunition equal to the penetrating number. Make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the initial target. If the attack hits, there is a creature within 15 feet of that creature and directly behind it, and the original {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} would hit the second creature, it also takes normal weapon damage. Alternatively, you can use this property to fire at a creature through partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}. When you do so, you reduce the target's {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} by one step (from three-quarters to half or half to one-quarter), rather than targeting a second creature.

entries.name: Piercing
entries: Before you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the piercing property, you can choose to gain a bonus to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} up to the piercing number. If you do so and you hit with it, you suffer an equivalent penalty to the damage roll.

entries.name: Powered
entries: While wearing armor with this property, your Strength score becomes equal to the powered number. If your Strength is already equal to or greater than the powered number, it has no effect on you.

entries.name: Reach
entries: A weapon with this property adds 5 feet to your reach with it.

entries.name: Range
entries: A weapon that can be used to make a ranged attack has this property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second indicates the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. You can't attack a target beyond the weapon's long range.

entries.name: Rapid
entries: When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with this property, you can instead unload on a single target, consuming ammunition equal to the rapid number. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon). On a failed save, roll the weapon's damage dice twice and add them together, adding relevant modifiers as normal and subjecting the target to any additional effects that would occur on a hit. If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Reactive
entries: When you are wearing armor with this property and a creature hits you with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you gain a bonus to AC against the next attack from that creature before the start of your next turn equal to the reactive number.

entries.name: Regulated
entries: When you are wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and a creature rolls the maximum on a weapon damage die against you, they must reroll and use the new roll, even if the new roll is the maximum on the weapon damage die.

entries.name: Returning
entries: When you throw a weapon with this property, it automatically returns to your hand after the attack is complete, whether you hit or miss.

entries.name: Rigid
entries: While wearing armor with this property, you add half your Dexterity modifier (rounded down), instead of your full Dexterity modifier, to Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} you make. If your Dexterity modifier is negative, you instead subtract the full modifier.

entries.name: Reload
entries: A number of shots equal to the reload number can be made with a weapon with this property. A character must then reload it using an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} (their choice). You must have one free hand to reload.

entries.name: Reinforced
entries: When you make a long jump while wearing armor with this property, you can {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} a number of feet up to twice your Strength score. When you make a high jump, you can leap a number of feet up into the air equal to 3 + twice your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Responsive
entries: While you are wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and an attack misses you by an amount less than or equal to your bonus to AC from your {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, you gain a bonus to AC against the next attack from that creature before the start of your next turn equal to the responsive number.

entries.name: Shocking
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon with the shocking property, you can force it to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the shocking number. On a failed save, the creature takes an additional 1d4 lightning damage and becomes {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Silent
entries: When you make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the silent property while hidden, it does not automatically reveal your presence. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check contested by your targets' Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check. On a success, you remain hidden.

entries.name: Slug cartridge
entries: Weapons with the {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge} property fire slug cartridges, which must be loaded in order to fire the weapon.

entries.name: Smart
entries: This weapon ignores your Dexterity score and {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. Two numbers appear in parentheses with the property—the first is the weapon's Dexterity score, and the second is the weapon's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. The weapon uses these values instead of yours when you make attack and damage rolls with it. If you lack proficiency with the weapon, the weapon does not benefit from its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Sonorous
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon with the sonorous property, you can force it to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the sonorous number. On a failed save, the creature takes an additional 1d4 sonic damage and becomes {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Special
entries: A weapon with this property has unusual rules governing its use, explained in the weapon's description (see "Special Weapons" later in this section).

entries.name: Specialized
entries: A weapon with this property bypasses the base and cap of certain properties. Another weapon property in parentheses with the property-the weapon property that the exotic bypasses the base and cap for.

entries.name: Spiked
entries: When you succeed on a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to shove or trip a creature while wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, the creature takes kinetic damage using the spiked damage (which appears in parentheses with the property) + your Strength modifier. If you use a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property as an improvised weapon, the damage increases by one step (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, or {@dice d8} to 2d4).

entries.name: Steadfast
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks and Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being moved.

entries.name: Strength
entries: A weapon with this property has a heavy kickback. While wielding it, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} unless you meet the Strength requirement. If the weapon has the burst, penetrating, or rapid property, you must meet the Strength requirement to use this feature. If the weapon lacks the two-handed property, you can wield the weapon in two hands to temporarily reduce the strength number by one step (from 19 to 17, 17 to 15, 15 to 13, or 13 to 11). If this would reduce the strength number below 11, you ignore it entirely.

entries.name: Two-Handed
entries: A weapon with this property requires two hands to use.

entries.name: Finesse
entries: When making an attack with a weapon with this property, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

entries.name: Heavy
entries: When you hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using Strength with a weapon with this property, you deal additional damage equal to half your Strength modifier (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Switch
entries: A weapon with the switch property can deal an alternate type of damage. A damage value appears in parentheses appears with the property-the damage when the weapon uses its alternate damage type. On your turn, you can use your object interaction to change the weapon's damage type.

entries.name: Light
entries: A weapon with this property is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when engaging in Double- or Two-Weapon Fighting. See the rules for Double- and Two-Weapon Fighting in chapter 9.

entries.name: Special
entries: A weapon with the special property has unusual rules governing its use, explained in the weapon's description (see "Special Weapons" later in this section).

entries.name: Thrown
entries: Weapons with this property can be thrown to make a ranged attack. If the weapon would normally be used to make melee weapon attacks, you use the same ability modifier for that {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon.

entries.name: Versatile
entries: A weapon with this property can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property—the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.

entries.name: Vicious
entries: Whenever you deal damage with a weapon with the vicious property and roll the maximum on a weapon damage die, you gain a bonus to damage equal to the vicious number.
